title: Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2611.07900v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Knowledge of the hidden interior structure of an object, including the presence and location of cavities, is essential for predictive simulation, robotic manipulation, and nondestructive inspection. However, such cavities leave no direct signature on the static visible surface, making collision-induced deformation one of the few cues used to infer their presence. Structure from Collision (SfC) addresses this problem by recovering the hidden interior structure of an object from multiview observations of a collision event. SfC is challenging for two reasons: hidden cavities are only indirectly observable through surface motion, and voids correspond to the absence of material, making direct optimization using standard density representations difficult. translated_title: 基于假设空间推理的碰撞结构恢复
translated_abstract: 了解物体的隐藏内部结构，包括空腔的存在与位置，对于预测性仿真、机器人操作和无损检测至关重要。然而，这类空腔在静态可见表面上不会留下任何直接痕迹，使得碰撞引起的变形成为推断其存在的少数线索之一。Structure from Collision（SfC）通过从碰撞事件的多视角观测中恢复物体的隐藏内部结构来解决这一问题。SfC 面临两大挑战：隐藏空腔只能通过表面运动间接观测，且空腔对应于材料的缺失，这使得使用标准密度表示进行直接优化变得困难。基于密度的 SfC 基线同时继承了这两个困难：表面匹配梯度无法直接指示空腔位置，而密度梯度在物体内部可能微弱或缺乏信息。
tldr: 提出通过假设空间推理从碰撞事件的多视角观测中恢复物体隐藏内部结构（如空腔），克服了空腔仅能通过表面运动间接观测、且因对应材料缺失而难以用密度表示直接优化的难题。
en_tdlr: Proposes recovering an object's hidden interior structure (e.g., cavities) from multiview observations of collision events via hypothesis-space reasoning, overcoming the challenges that cavities are only indirectly observable through surface motion and are difficult to optimize directly with standard density representations due to corresponding absence of material.
